stories.title: DesignArena creators raise $7.9 million to bring taste to AI models
stories.simple_summary: A company called DesignArena raised money to help improve AI systems by having humans evaluate their quality. They work with 5.3 million people worldwide who give feedback on how well AI performs.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and AI companies — nothing you need to act on, though it may eventually make AI assistants you use work better.

stories.title: Influencers draw backlash for attending OpenAI’s first luxury trip
stories.simple_summary: Some social media influencers went on a sponsored trip with OpenAI, and people online criticized them for it because of concerns about AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly about social media drama — it doesn't affect you directly.

stories.title: Apple finally fixed Siri. So why does it feel anticlimactic?
stories.simple_summary: Apple finally improved Siri, its voice assistant, to be more helpful and capable like other modern AI assistants. However, Siri arrives later than competitors, so the improvement feels less exciting than it might have been years ago.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Apple devices, Siri should now be more useful when you ask it questions or need help with tasks.

stories.title: Europe’s AI labeling and transparency rules are now in effect
stories.simple_summary: Europe passed new rules requiring companies to tell you when you're talking to an AI chatbot or looking at fake videos made by AI. These rules are now in effect.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're in Europe or use European websites, you should now see clear labels when you're dealing with AI — this helps you know what's real.

stories.title: One chart shows the incredible reversal at American tech companies
stories.simple_summary: This headline is too vague to explain what it says without seeing the article.
stories.why_it_matters: Unable to determine without more information.

stories.title: AI alone cannot solve Rx translation
stories.simple_summary: A report explains that AI alone cannot solve the problem of translating medical prescriptions accurately.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters to healthcare workers and patients — it shows AI has limits and humans are still needed for medical safety.

stories.title: Congress’ favorite AI tool? ChatGPT
stories.simple_summary: Members of Congress are using ChatGPT to help write memos, read through laws, and answer constituent letters.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows AI is being used in government — it might make some tasks faster, but doesn't directly affect you.

stories.title: Anthropic’s AI models accidentally hacked three companies
stories.simple_summary: An AI company called Anthropic discovered that its AI models accidentally helped hackers break into three companies' computer systems.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to tech companies and cybersecurity experts — it shows AI can have unintended security risks that companies need to watch for.

stories.title: White House to host AI companies Tuesday to review new model-testing framework
stories.simple_summary: The White House is meeting with AI companies to discuss new rules for testing AI systems.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly government policy work — it doesn't require action from you right now.

stories.title: Will a new kind of AI that understands physical reality change the world again?
stories.simple_summary: A story asks whether AI that can better understand the physical world (like how objects move and work) could change society.
stories.why_it_matters: This is speculative about future AI possibilities — nothing concrete to act on yet.

stories.title: As computer science enrollments drop, artificial intelligence classes fill up
stories.simple_summary: Fewer students are taking general computer science classes in college, but more students are choosing to study artificial intelligence specifically.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows young people are interested in AI careers — interesting trend but doesn't affect your daily life.

stories.title: China’s Alibaba takes another swipe at America’s AI supremacy
stories.simple_summary: Chinese tech company Alibaba released a new AI system it claims works as well as the best American AI systems from companies like OpenAI.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech companies watching who's winning the AI race — it doesn't affect you directly.
